actions.reason: b58encode's digit loop now takes two groups of four base-58 digits (two divmods by base**4) per iteration and appends all four pair lookups with a single list extend. This halves the loop-condition checks and list-extend operations per encoded character. If the second divmod passes the top of the integer, it produces only zero digits, and the existing lstrip of the zero character already removes them, so the output is byte-identical. Measured encode_ir ratio 0.9617 (decode_ir 0.9834, check_ir 0.9927). Equivalence harness identical, all tests pass.

candidate.patch:
diff --git a/base58/__init__.py b/base58/__init__.py
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -121,9 +121,13 @@ def b58encode(
     pairs, sq, big, zero = tables
     parts = []
     while i:
+        # Two groups of four digits per pass; a group past the top of i
+        # is all zero digits, which the lstrip below removes
         i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
         # rem is a small int: two operators are cheaper than a divmod call
-        parts += pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq]
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq])
     parts.reverse()
     return zero * (origlen - newlen) + b''.join(parts).lstrip(zero)
